pack.name: GDPR Compliance Baseline
pack.description: Privacy and data-protection architecture themes for cloud workloads — lawful basis, minimization, security of processing, DPIA triggers, and cross-border transfer safeguards. Thematic GDPR mapping only; not legal certification or statutory conformity assessment.

rules.title: Personal data encrypted at rest
rules.description: Datastores holding personal data must document encryption-at-rest expectations (platform-managed keys or customer-managed keys) so reviewers can assess Art. 32 security-of-processing posture.
rules.remediationGuidance: Record encryption expectations in governance.RequiredControls and datastores[].Tags; cite Azure SQL TDE, Storage SSE, or Cosmos encryption settings from resources.json when extractor inventory is present.

frameworkMappings.theme: Art. 32 — Security of processing (encryption at rest)

rules.title: Personal data encrypted in transit
rules.description: Service-to-service and client-to-service paths that carry personal data must assume TLS 1.2+ and document exceptions where legacy protocols remain.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document TLS minimums in governance.PolicyConstraints; align ReadsFrom/WritesTo relationship edges with HTTPS-only assumptions in metadata.ChangeDescription.

frameworkMappings.theme: Art. 32 — Security of processing (encryption in transit)

rules.title: Processing purpose documented per system
rules.description: Each system under review should state specific, explicit, and legitimate processing purposes — not generic catch-all language — so purpose-limitation can be assessed.
rules.remediationGuidance: Capture purpose statements in systemName narrative, services[].Purpose, and governance.ComplianceTags; avoid reuse of unrelated business purposes across workloads.

rules.title: Data minimization posture documented
rules.description: Architecture should explain why each personal-data field or datastore is necessary for the stated purpose; collection beyond need must be dispositioned or scoped out.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document field-level minimization rationale in governance.PolicyConstraints and metadata.ChangeDescription; tag non-essential datastores for exclusion or anonymization.

rules.title: Lawful basis for processing identified
rules.description: Manifest governance metadata should identify the lawful basis relied upon (contract, consent, legitimate interest, legal obligation, etc.) for material personal-data processing — counsel confirms applicability.
rules.remediationGuidance: Add lawful-basis tags to governance.ComplianceTags (e.g., lawful-basis:contract) and cross-reference processing purposes in metadata.ChangeDescription.

rules.title: Records of processing activities (ROPA) themes documented
rules.description: Architecture evidence should support ROPA-style inventory: processing purposes, data categories, recipients, retention, and cross-border transfer notes at system scope.
rules.remediationGuidance: Mirror ROPA fields in governance.RequiredControls or attached metadata.ChangeDescription tables; enumerate datastores[] and external services that receive personal data.

rules.title: DPIA trigger assessment documented for high-risk processing
rules.description: Where processing is likely high risk (systematic monitoring, large-scale special-category data, automated decisions with legal effect), architecture should document whether a DPIA was performed or why one was not required.
rules.remediationGuidance: Record DPIA status and summary conclusions in governance.PolicyConstraints; link DecisionTraceIds when DPIA outcomes informed design choices.

rules.title: EU/EEA data residency and transfer constraints stated
rules.description: When personal data of EU/EEA data subjects is processed, architecture must document primary storage regions and any transfers outside the EEA with safeguard themes (SCCs, adequacy, BCRs).
rules.remediationGuidance: Tag region constraints on datastores[].Tags and governance.ComplianceTags; document transfer mechanisms in governance.PolicyConstraints when US or other third-country services appear in services[].

rules.title: Retention periods defined for personal data stores
rules.description: Each personal-data datastore should have documented retention and deletion schedules aligned to purpose limitation — indefinite retention requires explicit justification.
rules.remediationGuidance: Encode retention windows in governance.PolicyConstraints and datastores[].Tags; reference backup retention separately where archives extend beyond operational retention.

rules.title: Pseudonymisation applied where feasible
rules.description: Architectures processing personal data at scale should document pseudonymisation or tokenisation strategies for analytics, logs, and non-production environments.
rules.remediationGuidance: Describe pseudonymisation approach in governance.PolicyConstraints; tag analytics pipelines and log sinks that must not hold direct identifiers.

rules.title: Privacy-by-design defaults documented
rules.description: New features and data flows should default to the most privacy-protective settings (opt-in where appropriate, minimal collection, restricted sharing) unless documented otherwise.
rules.remediationGuidance: Capture default-deny sharing and collection posture in governance.RequiredControls; align services[].RequiredControls with privacy defaults.

frameworkMappings.theme: Art. 25 — Data protection by design and by default

rules.title: Access controls on personal data stores
rules.description: Role-based access to personal-data datastores must follow least privilege; broad admin or shared credentials on production personal-data paths require documented exceptions.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document RBAC and entitlement models in governance.RequiredControls; cite Entra ID / database RBAC posture from extractor IAM exports when available.

rules.title: Audit logging for personal data access
rules.description: Systems processing personal data should document who accessed what and when — centralized audit sinks and retention for access logs must be described.
rules.remediationGuidance: Reference Log Analytics, database auditing, or SIEM integration in services[].Tags and governance.RequiredControls; note retention alignment with Art. 5 storage limitation.

frameworkMappings.theme: Art. 32 — Security of processing (logging and monitoring)

rules.title: Personal data breach detection capability
rules.description: Architecture should describe how unauthorised access, exfiltration, or integrity failures affecting personal data would be detected in time to meet breach-notification timelines.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document alerting paths and incident hooks in governance.RequiredControls; tie monitoring services to datastores holding personal data via relationship edges.

frameworkMappings.theme: Art. 33 — Notification of a personal data breach

rules.title: Processors and subprocessors documented
rules.description: Third-party services that process personal data on the controller's behalf must appear in architecture with processing role, data categories, and contractual safeguard themes.
rules.remediationGuidance: Enumerate processor services in services[] with Purpose and Tags indicating processor role; reference DPA/SCC status in governance.PolicyConstraints.

rules.title: Cross-border transfer safeguards documented
rules.description: When personal data leaves the EEA, architecture must name the transfer tool relied upon (SCCs, adequacy decision, derogation themes) — not merely the destination country.
rules.remediationGuidance: Add transfer-mechanism tags to governance.ComplianceTags for each non-EEA service or region; document supplementary measures where required by counsel.

frameworkMappings.theme: Art. 46 — Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards

rules.title: Data subject access request (DSAR) architecture
rules.description: Systems should document how access requests (Art. 15) are fulfilled — locate, export, and redact personal data across stores and services within operational SLAs.
rules.remediationGuidance: Describe DSAR workflow and datastore coverage in governance.PolicyConstraints; tag systems participating in subject-rights fulfillment.

rules.title: Erasure and right-to-be-forgotten mechanics
rules.description: Architecture must explain how erasure requests propagate across primary stores, caches, backups, and downstream processors — including backup retention trade-offs.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document deletion cascades and backup handling in governance.PolicyConstraints; flag long-retention archives that complicate erasure.

rules.title: Consent management architecture where consent is basis
rules.description: If consent is the lawful basis, architecture should show how consent is captured, stored, withdrawn, and propagated to processing systems.
rules.remediationGuidance: Tag consent-reliant flows in governance.ComplianceTags; document consent record store and withdrawal propagation in metadata.ChangeDescription.

rules.title: Special category data extra safeguards
rules.description: Processing of special-category personal data (health, biometric, etc.) requires documented additional safeguards and explicit lawful-basis themes beyond ordinary personal data.
rules.remediationGuidance: Tag special-category datastores and flows in governance.ComplianceTags; document Art. 9 condition relied upon and enhanced controls in governance.RequiredControls.

rules.title: Data portability export capability
rules.description: Where portability applies, architecture should describe structured, machine-readable export paths for data subjects without undue delay.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document export APIs or batch export jobs in services[].Purpose and governance.PolicyConstraints; note format standards (JSON, CSV) where defined.

rules.title: Automated decision-making transparency
rules.description: Systems using solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects must document logic, significance, and human-review override paths.
rules.remediationGuidance: Tag ML/inference services in services[].Tags; document human-in-the-loop and explanation posture in governance.PolicyConstraints.

rules.title: Children's data protections documented
rules.description: If children's personal data may be processed, architecture should document age-verification and parental-authorisation themes appropriate to the service context.
rules.remediationGuidance: Flag child-directed or youth-facing flows in governance.ComplianceTags; document age-gate and consent mechanics in governance.PolicyConstraints.

rules.title: Privacy notice linkage at collection points
rules.description: Collection surfaces should reference where data subjects receive Art. 13–14 transparency information — architecture should map systems to notice delivery channels.
rules.remediationGuidance: Document privacy-notice URLs or in-app disclosure flows in services[].Tags and metadata.ChangeDescription.

rules.title: DPO and privacy contact themes documented
rules.description: Where a DPO is appointed or privacy contact is required, architecture documentation should include reachable contact paths for data-subject and supervisory-authority inquiries.
rules.remediationGuidance: Record DPO or privacy-office contact references in governance.PolicyConstraints or metadata.ChangeDescription.

rules.title: Non-production environments use pseudonymised or synthetic data
rules.description: Lower environments should not rely on production personal data unless documented exceptions with compensating controls exist.
rules.remediationGuidance: Tag non-prod datastores and services with environment class and data-sanitisation approach in services[].Tags and datastores[].Tags.

rules.title: Backup encryption and retention aligned to privacy policy
rules.description: Backup and archive tiers holding personal data must document encryption and retention that does not undermine erasure or storage-limitation commitments.
rules.remediationGuidance: Describe backup encryption and restore-test cadence in governance.RequiredControls; align backup retention tags with gdpr-009 retention narrative.

frameworkMappings.theme: Art. 32 and Art. 5(1)(e) — Backup security and storage limitation

rules.title: Third-party API data sharing disclosed in architecture
rules.description: Outbound integrations that share personal data with partners or SaaS APIs must be enumerated with purpose, categories, and recipient identity — not hidden in generic integration lists.
rules.remediationGuidance: List external recipients on WritesTo relationship edges and services[]; document sharing purpose in services[].Purpose and governance.ComplianceTags.

frameworkMappings.theme: Art. 13–14 and Art. 28 — Recipient disclosure and processor transparency
